title: page-slicing adaptive evictor and KV heap harmonizer
author: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Context: On heavy multi-tenant inference workloads we observed increased fragmentation of the KV cache under mixed sequence length distributions and continuous batching. Fragmentation coupled with conservative spill thresholds caused unnecessary spillover to disk and cross-tenant eviction storms during transient load spikes. This PR introduces a coordinated suite of changes: 1) a page-slicing allocator that exposes page-granular slices within large allocations to reduce internal fragmentation for variable-sized "slices"; 2) an adaptive evictor that combines age, page-contiguity score, and tenant pressure signals to make eviction decisions that minimize future page splits and I/O; and 3) a KV heap harmonizer which smooths tenant reservations and performs cheap local compactions (page coalescing) asynchronously to avoid synchronous stalls.

Design highlights: The page-slicer retains the existing slab-based fast path but splits large pages into variable-sized "slices" with compact metadata stored in a compact descriptor array. Slice allocation is lock-free on the fast path and falls back to a per-shard serializer for rare compaction cases. The adaptive evictor computes an eviction priority p = alpha * age_score + beta * fragmentation_penalty + gamma * tenant_pressure with tunable weights and hysteresis; it biases toward evicting items whose eviction will free contiguous slices and avoid creating remote spill fragments. The harmonizer periodically runs a cooperative compaction: it identifies small free slices adjacent to allocated slices and issues in-place nanomoves to coalesce live data, using an optimistic write-lock to avoid interfering with KV reads. Compaction is bounded by a cpu_budget and IO_budget to preserve latency SLOs.

Safety and operational behavior: - The new allocator and harmonizer have feature gates (kv.page_slicer_enabled, kv.harmonizer_budget_ms) so operators can roll out gradually. - Eviction thresholds are tenant-aware: tenants can set soft and hard watermarks; the evictor ramps aggressiveness between them. - To prevent cascading evictions, the evictor implements a backoff window that temporarily shields recently-evicted tenants from re-eviction for a short period. - Spillover remains available as a fallback; this PR improves spill granularity to prefer spilling contiguous segments rather than many small keys to reduce downstream read amplification.

Benchmarks: Microbench (1000 concurrent sessions, mixed seq lens 32/256/1024): - Average memory utilization improved by ~12% due to reduced fragmentation. - Spill frequency decreased by 24% (measured spill events per minute). - P99 generation latency reduced by ~18% under peak load due to fewer synchronous compactions and fewer remote spills. - End-to-end throughput held steady or slightly improved (+3%) because batching kernels benefited from better locality.

Changes included: - New allocator and metadata descriptors (src/runtime/kv/page_slicer.rs, include/svc/kv/page_slicer.h) - Adaptive evictor implementation and strategy hooks (src/runtime/kv/evictor.rs) - Harmonizer background worker and tuning knobs (src/runtime/kv/harmonizer.rs) - Scheduler integration: the evictor now signals the continuous-batching scheduler to re-evaluate batch formation when significant compaction completes (src/runtime/scheduler/batching.rs) - Kernel selector hinting: added a lightweight locality hint for token-level kernels to prefer kernels optimized for contiguous KV access patterns (src/runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.rs) - Tests and benchmarks (tests/kv/eviction_integration.rs, benches/kv_fragmentation_bench.rs) - Docs and tuning guide (docs/perf/kv-page-slicing.md)

Testing: Unit tests cover slice allocation/free, boundary conditions, and evictor scoring. Integration tests simulate tenant isolation and ensure harmonizer compactions do not violate correctness. Benchmarks were run in the perf-lab cluster for representative sizes. CI: full test matrix passed; the bench workflow ran as a post-merge job (results attached in CI artifacts).

Checklist: - [x] Feature-gated and defaults preserve current behavior - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks in perf-lab - [x] Observability (metrics added for slice fragmentation, harmonizer compactions, eviction reasons) - [x] Doc updates and tuning guide - [x] Backwards-compatible on-disk format (spill format unchanged)

Related work: follows up on earlier eviction and compaction efforts (see ENG-2145 and ENG-2714). This PR intentionally avoids broad slab refactors; instead it targets a lower-risk page-slicing surface that can be toggled at runtime.

Operational notes: On rollout, enable the page_slicer in a canary pool for 24–72 hours, monitor kv.slice_fragmentation_ratio and kv.spill_rate, then expand. Harmonizer defaults to a conservative cpu_budget_ms=2 and io_budget=8MB/s per shard to avoid contention.

review_conversation: Alex Chen (reviewer): Can you expand on the harmonizer's locking model? I worry about read latency if compaction takes the fast-path lock.

Maya Rodriguez (author): Harmonizer uses optimistic write-locks and only takes the fast-path serializer for rare boundary moves. Added comments and a microbenchmark showing <0.25ms median extra read latency when harmonizer is active.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): The eviction scoring adds new telemetry tags; please make sure high-cardinality tags are avoided.
Maya Rodriguez (author): Switched tenant_pressure to a low-cardinality bucketed enum and added documentation for tags. Also throttled harmonizer by default to minimize tag churn.
Jonas Meyer (reviewer): Could the scheduler hint create oscillation between kernels?
Maya Rodriguez (author): The hint is advisory and decays over time; scheduler has damping to avoid thrash. Expanded tests to simulate oscillation scenarios.
Alex Chen (approver): Verified bench results and test coverage. Approving.
Priya Kapoor (approver): Approved after telemetry changes and docs.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory efficiency and reduces spill frequency by introducing a page-slicing allocator, an adaptive eviction policy, and a background harmonizer for low-latency compaction. Feature-gated and safe to roll out incrementally.
